LESSON: MONEY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Measurement 2.4 Time (10 lessons) By the end of the sub-strand, the learner shou
Topic 2.5: Money
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Money, part of Measurement 2.4 Time (10 lessons) By the end of the sub-strand, the learner shou in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: How do you represent same amount of money using different denominations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms related to Kenyan currency.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify Kenyan currency coins and notes up to sh.100,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. count the number of sh. 10 and sh. 20 coins in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. count the number of sh. 50 and sh. 100 notes in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. add two denominations of money with a sum not exceeding sh. 100,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. use money to buy up to 3 items without balance,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

G. appreciate the use of money in buying items. ● Learners in pairs or groups are guided to identify, fingerspell, sign and sort out Kenyan currency notes according to their value up to sh.1000 i.e. sh. 5 coin, sh 10 coin, sh 20 coin, sh 50 note, sh 100 note and balance. ● In pairs or groups, recognize and sort out Kenyan currency coins and notes up to sh.100. ● In groups, make sh. 10 and sh. 20 coins paper cut-outs, sort and count the number of sh. 10 and sh. 20 coins paper cut-outs. ● In groups, make sh. 50 and sh. 100 notes paper cut-outs, sort and count the number of sh. 50 and sh. 100 notes paper cut-outs. ● Add two denominations of money with a sum not exceeding sh. 100. ● In pairs or groups, role play buying up to 3 items without balance from the model shop in the classroom. ● Record a video during a role play of classroom shopping activities. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Money together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: Information and communication skills communicates and collaborates with their peers, in pairs or in groups

counting Kenyan currency notes in different denominations up to sh100 using imitation money.

Values:
• Patriotism: Learners dedicate while working in pairs or groups sort out Kenyan currency notes according to their value up to

sh.1000.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Financial literacy: The choice of what to buy and what not to buy as learners in groups role play buying up to 3 items involving

balance using imitation money up to sh.1000 in shopping activities.

Link to other learning areas:

• Learners relate skills on buying and shopping activities in Language activities.

Suggested Learning resources:

● Kenyan currency coins and notes or imitations up to sh.1000, classroom shop, digital devices
